tasks.instructions: The first table below shows changes in the total population of New York City from 1800 to 2000. The second and third tables show changes in the population of the five districts of the city (Manhattan, Brooklyn, Bronx, Queens, Staten Island) over the same period. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

visual_data.title: New York City (all five districts)
visual_data.description: Total population figures for New York City across three centuries: 1800 (79,216); 1900 (3,437,202); 2000 (8,009,185).

visual_data.title: Manhattan
visual_data.description: Manhattan's population and its percentage share of the total NYC population: 1800 (60,515 residents, 76%); 1900 (1,850,093 residents, 54%); 2000 (1,538,096 residents, 19%).

visual_data.title: Other districts (Brooklyn, Bronx, Queens, Staten Island)
visual_data.description: Combined population and percentage share for Brooklyn, Bronx, Queens, and Staten Island: 1800 (18,701 residents, 24%); 1900 (1,587,109 residents, 46%); 2000 (6,471,089 residents, 81%).

tasks.instructions: The plans below show the site of a farm in 1950 and the same site today. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

visual_data.title: Beechwood Farm in 1950
visual_data.description: Original farm layout: Large areas for sheep (North East), Fruit trees, Soft fruits, and Vegetables. Infrastructure includes a barn, farmhouse, and chicken area. All sections are connected by simple tracks.

visual_data.title: Beechwood Farm Today
visual_data.description: Modernized layout: Sheep area replaced by a camping field and solar panels. A farm shop and parking have been added near the fruit trees. The barn is now a smaller structure, and new holiday cottages have been built. The original tracks have been upgraded to roads.

tasks.instructions: The diagram below shows how fabric is manufactured from bamboo. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

visual_data.title: How bamboo fabric is made
visual_data.description: A 9-step process diagram: 1) Plant bamboo plants (Spring); 2) Harvest (Autumn); 3) Cut into strips; 4) Crush strips (to make liquid pulp); 5) Filter (separate long fibres from liquid); 6) Soften fibres (add water and amine oxide); 7) Spin (to make yarn); 8) Weave (to make fabric); 9) Final products (such as t-shirts and socks).
